entityDescription: The Extrapolation Factory is a design-based research studio for participatory futures studies, founded by Elliott P. Montgomery and Chris Woebken. The studio develops experimental methods for collaboratively prototyping, experiencing and impacting future scenarios. Central to these methods is the creation of hypothetical future props and their deployment in familiar contexts such as 99¢ stores, science museums, vending machines and city sidewalks. With this work, the studio is exploring new territories for democratized futures by rapidly imagining, prototyping, deploying and evaluating visions of possible futures on an extended time scale. The Core77 Design Award was granted to The Extrapolation Factory in 2013’s Speculative Design category and the Extrapolation Factory was nominated for the Design Museum’s Designs of the Year award in 2015.

entityDescription: MetGIS GmbH is a spin-off of the University of Vienna, specialized in the automated operational calculation of ultra high resolution world-wide weather forecasts. In contrast to the common standard, extra precise terrain data are included in the forecast generation process, resulting in a supreme quality of the calculated predictions, especially over mountain areas. MetGIS realtime predictions are available via www.metgis.com, but are also provided in form of APIs (application programming interfaces). These allow providers of foreign information systems (websites, apps, etc.) to access weather predictions not only for individual points, but also as color map overlays, zoomable to resolutions of less than 100 m for many parts of the world. The international customers stem from fields such as tourism, avalanche warning, open-pit mining and wintry road maintenance. Amongst others, they profit from the more cost-effective planning of resources and the possibility to lower the weather-related risk of accidents.

entityDescription:
Gold Mobile Innovation (GMI) Ltd is a small innovation consultancy with deep experience in the mobile and digital industries. Founded in 2007, GMI has been increasingly specialising in Open Innovation, Open R&D, and collaborative product & service development models, leading to the creation of The Mobile Collective (TMC) in 2010. TMC enables and supports the collaborative development of innovative technology-based solutions by bringing the mobile developer & designer communities together with professional scientists and educators in ThinkCamp events. ThinkCamps provide an open and creative environment for developing new products and services. They are designed to support a collaborative approach to generating cross-industry solutions. The events select one area of focus (such as Citizen Science ) and are structured to address problems, rise to challenges, and take advantage of new opportunities. Participants are drawn from a diverse range of disciplines and skill-sets, which they apply in a creative way. The TMC team facilitates the generation of ideas during the ThinkCamp events and then provides support for the organically formed working groups to further develop and implement the solutions, both during and beyond the event. 

The TMC team also has 8 years experience in running Hack Days, primarily Over the Air (www.overtheair.org), which has been the largest and most successful developer event in the Mobile Industry. Over the Air has typically attracted over 600 attendees and the active support of major players in the mobile industry. A key feature of every Over the Air is the Hack Day competition, which attracts over 20 entries each year – many of which win valuable prizes across a wide range of general categories, sponsored categories, and thematic or problem-solving challenges. At the record breaking 2011 event held in Bletchley Park, more than 120 attendees stayed coding overnight. 

Most recently, TMC was a consortium member in the EU FP7-funded Citizen Cyberlab project, whose goals were to to build digital tools and online collaborative platforms for Citizen Science, and to enhance the opportunities for learning and creativity available to Citizen Scientists world wide. Within this project, TMC led the community outreach and engagement activities (including running events such as Hack Days and Code Sprints) across the development of 7 platforms and tools for Citizen Science and 4 pilot projects, led the development of requirements with respect to learning and community building and building community engagement, and supported dissemination and exploitation planning throughout the project.

entityDescription: The Arηs Group, founded in 2003, is a fully independent group of companies active in Europe, specialized in delivering solutions for complex IT systems. It is composed of Arηs Developments (Luxembourg), Arηs Developments Belgium (Brussels), Arηs Developments Hellas Information Systems (Athens), Arηs Developments Italia (Milan), Arηs Consulting (Luxembourg), Arηs Cube (Luxembourg), Arηs Digital (Brussels), Arηs Spikeseed (Luxembourg) and Arηs Technology (Leuven). The Group is specialized in IT services for large organisations. The focus is on state-of-the-art software development, business intelligence, digital trust, enterprise architecture and infrastructure services. The expertise covers several domains like web portals (including open data portals), mobile applications, digital signature, trans-European systems, semantic search layers, e-Government, and operation of IT systems. With more than 1000 consultants, the Arηs Group proposes to its customers a specific and competitive delivery model on a fixed price basis, a time and means mode on- and off-site or a fully managed service with a 24/7 Service Level Agreement. Moreover, Arηs has clearly become an example of Centre of Excellence in Software Engineering, combining top educated resources with highly professional processes and tools. This was endorsed in 2013, following the CMMI appraisal of Arηs Developments, Arηs Developments Belgium and Arηs Spikeseed at the level 2 of the Capability Maturity Model Integration of the CMMI Institute. In 2013, Arηs Cube had also the PSF approval as "Operator of Communication Networks and Secondary Computer Systems in the Financial Sector". The Arηs Group is ISO 9001:2008 certified since 2009.

entityDescription:
Geminali AS

Geminali AS was established in 1998. The goal of the company and its partner company Geminor Inc, USA is to develop and commercialise software tools and instrumentation in the areas of environmental optics, radiative transfer, and remote sensing as well as to market instruments produced by collaborative partners. 

The company has done world wide marketing of instruments developed and produced by the Norwegian Institute for Air Research (NILU) for measurements of UV radiation and visible light together with software for estimating biological dose rates, total ozone column amount, cloud effects, and surface albedo. In addition, the company is actively engaged in the development of algorithms for interpretation of satellite remote sensing data through tight collaboration with the University of Bergen, Norway and Stevens Institute of Technology, USA. 

With funding from the Norwegian Research Council (NRC) and the Norwegian Space Centre (NSC), the company is actively involved in projects to develop retrieval algorithms associated with optical satellite remote sensing of open oceans, icy arctic waters, coastal waters, lakes, and snow-covered surfaces. 

Our partner company, Geminor Inc, USA, has recently developed a software tool (AccuRT) for accurate an efficient computation of radiative transfer in coupled atmosphere-surface systems. This software tool will play an important role in the proposed development of an Inherent Optical Properties algorithm for the Sentinel-3 OLCI sensor.

For the last twenty years Geminali AS and Geminor Inc have been heavily involved in research related to the retrieval of aerosol and marine IOPs with projects involving both theoretical algorithm development and fieldwork to acquire marine in situ data for algorithm validation. Fieldwork has included projects funded by NRC and NSC in Norway, Africa, and China, and algorithm development has included projects for NASA, ESA, JAXA (Japan), and KIOST (South Korea). The work for JAXA is aimed at retrieval of snow properties, while the work for South Korea involves development of algorithms for cloud screening, atmospheric correction, and IOP retrieval using data from the upcoming GOCI-II geostationary satellite.

entityDescription:
Evince Technology is an SME company developing a highly novel new class of devices based on synthetic diamond. Rather than employ conventional semiconductor approaches, Evince has instead developed processes to embed highly enhanced field emission sources within the diamond. This yields a family of patented electron devices (using diamond as a solid-state vacuum) as well as a highly robust cold cathode electron source that does not suffer from the usual degradation mechanisms because the emitters are fully encapsulated within the diamond.
Being based on diamond, the devices will be inherently hard to radiation and robust over a wide temperature range. The technology has multiple near term space applications such as electron sources for TWT’s and ion thrusters, and longer term application in solid-state power electronic and high frequency amplifier components.

entityDescription:
INFALIA is a spin-off company of the MKLab (https://mklab.iti.gr/) group of Centre for Research and Technology Hellas (CERTH) – Information Technologies Institute (ITI), focusing on AI and semantic technologies on images, videos, text and multimodal content. MKLab, for more than 17 years, has machine learning expertise in several domains of application, through its leading role in an extensive list of European projects, where it participates or coordinates (https://mklab.iti.gr/projects). 

In the space domain, MKLab technically coordinates the H2020-EOPEN project (https://eopen-project.eu/), under the H2020-EO-2-2017 EO Big Data shift topic. In EOPEN, MKLab is responsible for the domains of knowledge discovery and knowledge representation. AI and Machine learning methods are followed in change, concept and event detection from EO and non-EO data. Clustering techniques identify and visualise key-players and user communities in the corresponding use case domain. An advanced multimodal fusion approach is also introduced to quantify similarities among heterogeneous multimodal objects to assist information retrieval. In addition, the participating team is responsible for the creation of the EOPEN ontology to provide automatic semantic reasoning for decision making. These tasks also require involvement in the linking of EO data with non-EO data and external open data sources. Furthermore, the MKLab team is responsible for crawling data from the Web and Social Media sources and will also be responsible for the Web presence of EOPEN and other communication activities. The project involves three pilot use case scenarios in monitoring flood, climate change and food security.
